title: Putting a Figure on a Technician's Finding Against Equipment Rental and Demo Kit
content:
## Where this applies

An item of hire kit from the Equipment Rental and Demo line that a technician has found fault with is assessed against the agreement it was hired on, one assessment for each item. A finding entered when kit was checked back in stands on the agreement's rental account at nil until it is assessed, and this is the basis on which the amount the guest bears for that finding is settled and written onto it.

Two findings on one agreement are two assessments, each worked and entered on its own.

Fair wear on edges and bases is not charged, and kit that never comes back is charged at the package's replacement value rather than assessed under this basis.

## What the assessment does

Writing the figure onto the finding raises the amount still to be collected on the agreement the entry belongs to by the same figure. Once it is done, the guest sees the figure against that finding on the agreement's rental account, and the agreement's outstanding figure carries it.

## Recording the assessment

The entry is made with the hidden tool `assess_returned_kit_damage_f0dbd642`. It belongs to the guest services agent: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. One call puts a figure on one finding.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `rental_event_id` | An identifier: the reference number of the technician's finding entry on the rental account that is being assessed, read from the rental account entry lookup before the call. It identifies the one item and the fault found on it. |
| `damage_charge_usd` | A fixed-format amount: the amount the guest is being asked to bear for that finding, in USD to 2 decimal places, rounded half up at the last step only. Where nothing is being asked of the guest, 0.00 is passed. |

Neither parameter carries an enumerated set of values; each takes the one value the record or the working gives it.

### What comes back

A plain-language confirmation naming the finding entry that was assessed, the agreement it belongs to, the amount written onto it and the agreement's outstanding figure after the assessment. Receiving that confirmation is what indicates the assessment was written; the figure is then readable on the agreement's rental account.

## Points of judgement

**One item, one call.** Because the finding is recorded against the item rather than against the agreement as a whole, an agreement carrying two faulted items is assessed by two calls, each naming its own finding entry.

**A finding that costs the guest nothing.** The figure passed is 0.00, and the finding is assessed at that.
